---
title: FFTLog
---

This page describes the logarithmic Fast Fourier Transform implemented by the
abstract [[numcosmo-math|NcmFftlog]] class. It computes the FFT of a function
assumed to be a periodic sequence of logarithmically spaced points, following
the FFTLog approach of @Hamilton2000 with the extensions described below.

## Decomposition

A function $G(r)$ is written as
$$
G(r) = \int_0^\infty F(k)\,K(kr)\,\mathrm{d}k, \tag{1}
$$
where $F(k)$ is defined in the fundamental interval
$[\ln k_0 - L/2,\ \ln k_0 + L/2]$, $L$ is the period, $\ln k_0$ the center value,
and $K(kr)$ a kernel function. Assuming $F(k)$ can be written in terms of the $N$
lowest Fourier modes,
$$
F(k) = \sum_n c_n\,e^{\frac{2\pi i n}{L}\ln\left(\frac{k}{k_0}\right)}.
$$
Substituting into Eq. (1) and changing variables $k \rightarrow t = kr$,
$$
\begin{aligned}
r G(r) &= \sum_n c_n \int_0^\infty \left(\frac{k}{k_0}\right)^{\frac{2\pi i n}{L}} K(kr)\,\mathrm{d}(kr) \\
       &= \sum_n c_n \int_0^\infty \left(\frac{t}{k_0 r}\right)^{\frac{2\pi i n}{L}} K(t)\,\mathrm{d}t \\
       &= \sum_n c_n\,e^{-\frac{2\pi i n}{L}\ln\left(\frac{r}{r_0}\right)}\,e^{-\frac{2\pi i n}{L}\ln(k_0 r_0)}\,Y_n,
\end{aligned}
$$
where
$$
Y_n = \int_0^\infty t^{\frac{2\pi i n}{L}} K(t)\,\mathrm{d}t,
$$
and the Fourier coefficients are
$$
c_n = \frac{1}{N}\sum_m F(k_m)\,e^{-\frac{2\pi i n m}{N}}.
$$
The total number of points $N$ is the number of knots in the fundamental
interval, which are equally spaced.

## Discretization

The variable discretization differs depending on whether $N$ is even or odd; in
general
$$
k_n = k_0\,\mathrm{e}^{n L / N}, \qquad r_m = r_0\,\mathrm{e}^{m L / N}.
$$
If $N$ is odd, $n$ and $m$ run over $[-\lfloor N/2\rfloor, \lfloor N/2\rfloor]$,
where $\lfloor N/2\rfloor$ is the round-down of $N/2$. In this case
$$
\begin{aligned}
\ln\left(k_{-\lfloor N/2\rfloor}\right) &= \ln(k_0) - \frac{N-1}{N}\frac{L}{2}, \\
\ln\left(k_{+\lfloor N/2\rfloor}\right) &= \ln(k_0) + \frac{N-1}{N}\frac{L}{2},
\end{aligned}
$$
so for odd $N$ the values of $k_n$ (and $r_n$) never touch the borders
$\ln(k_0) \pm L/2$ and $\ln(r_0) \pm L/2$. For even $N$
($\lfloor N/2\rfloor = N/2$),
$$
\begin{aligned}
\ln\left(k_{-\lfloor N/2\rfloor}\right) &= \ln(k_0) - \frac{L}{2}, \\
\ln\left(k_{+\lfloor N/2\rfloor}\right) &= \ln(k_0) + \frac{L}{2}.
\end{aligned}
$$
Since the functions are assumed periodic with period $L$, these two points refer
to the same value. We therefore include only the lower end point
$\ln(k_0) - L/2$ for even $N$. The original FFTLog paper includes both points with
a $1/2$ weight; using only the lower end point avoids that complication.

## Padding

Because the algorithm assumes the decomposed function is periodic, it is worth
extending the interval in $\ln k$ with padding intervals
$\left[\ln k_0 - \frac{L_T}{2},\ \ln k_0 - \frac{L}{2}\right)$ and
$\left(\ln k_0 + \frac{L}{2},\ \ln k_0 + \frac{L_T}{2}\right]$, where the total
period $L_T$ is set by the final number of knots, about $N(1 + \mathrm{padding})$.
The $N$ fundamental knots are equally distributed, and about $N \times \mathrm{padding}$
knots are placed in the two symmetric padding intervals; the exact split is given in the
section on the size below.

By default the padding holds zeros. When $F$ does not vanish at an end of the
interval this puts a step into the periodic input, and the transform rings at $r$
near the inverse of that end at a level that falls only as $1/N$, so a calibration
of $N$ on the whole output grid never converges. With
[[numcosmo-math|ncm_fftlog_use_smooth_padding]] the padding continues the input
instead: each end is continued by its power law, with the value and log-slope of
$F$ at the end taken from a cubic through the four nearest knots and anchored at
the end itself, so that the continuation does not move with the knots; an end where
$F k$ would grow along the continuation is cut by a Gaussian in $\ln k$ of width the
inverse of that log-slope; and each continuation is tapered to zero by a $C^\infty$ step
over $[0.4\,h, 0.8\,h]$ from its own end, with $h = pL/2$ the nominal padding of each
side, so the two ends never meet and the taper does not move when a fractional padding
rounds to a different period at each size. The periodic input is then continuous with its first
derivative at each end of the interval, where the continuation matches the value and
log-slope of $F$ but not its higher derivatives, and smooth elsewhere; the transform
converges as about $N^{-3}$ over the whole grid, down to a roundoff floor: for the
Eisenstein--Hu case below the change per doubling of $N$ is $8.1 \times 10^{-10}$,
$5.7 \times 10^{-11}$ and $1.2 \times 10^{-11}$ from 1000 to 8000 knots. The result within a few e-foldings of
$1/k_\mathrm{max}$ or $1/k_\mathrm{min}$ depends on the continuation, which is an
extrapolation of $F$ beyond its interval: for the $\sigma^2(R)$ of an
Eisenstein--Hu spectrum tabulated on $[10^{-6}, 10^3]$ (padding one, 6000 knots), the
power-law continuation is off the spectrum's own extension by $3.1 \times 10^{-4}$ of the
peak at $R = 1/k_\mathrm{max}$, $2.5 \times 10^{-8}$ at $10/k_\mathrm{max}$ and
$1.2 \times 10^{-9}$ at $100/k_\mathrm{max}$.

### Reach of the continuation

Beyond $0.8\,h$ from each end the padded input is zero, so the transform computes the
integral of $F$ continued over at most $0.8\,h$ e-folds past each end of the table, and
leaves out the rest. What that costs depends on how fast $F k$, the integrand in $\ln k$,
falls beyond the ends:

- For $F = k^2 P(k) / (2\pi^2)$ of a physical spectrum, $F k$ falls as $k^{3 + n_s}$
  below $k_\mathrm{min}$, so the low-$k$ part left out is negligible. Above
  $k_\mathrm{max}$, $F k$ is nearly flat ($\propto k^{n_s - 1}$ up to logarithms) and the
  kernel's own decay, $t^{-4}$ for the top-hat, makes the part left out negligible except
  within a few e-foldings of $1/k_\mathrm{max}$, as in the Eisenstein--Hu figures above.
- For an input whose $F k$ falls slowly beyond an end, the missing part is felt over the
  whole grid and grows toward that edge. For the top-hat window and $F \propto k^{-0.6}$
  on $[10^{-10}, 10^{3}]$ with padding one ($F k \propto k^{0.4}$ below $k_\mathrm{min}$),
  $G$ is off the power law continued to $k = 0$ by $6 \times 10^{-6}$ at
  $k_\mathrm{min} r = 10^{-9}$, $2.4 \times 10^{-4}$ at $10^{-5}$ and $1.5 \times 10^{-3}$
  at $10^{-3}$.

Any reference for such an input is itself an extrapolation of the table. When an
application needs it further, the levers are, in order of cost:

1. **A longer padding.** The taper scales with $h = pL/2$, so a larger padding fraction
   carries the continuation proportionally further, at the price of more knots.
2. **A wider table.** Tabulating $P(k)$ beyond the range of interest removes the
   extrapolation from the result altogether.
3. **The taper placement.** The window $[0.4\,h, 0.8\,h]$ is set in
   `_ncm_fftlog_add_smooth_padding()`. A later, narrower taper keeps more of a slow tail:
   with $[0.65\,h, 0.95\,h]$, the Gaussian window and $F \propto k^{-1/2}$ on
   $[10^{-8}, 10^3]$ are off $\Gamma(1/4) / (2\sqrt{r})$ by $2.3 \times 10^{-4}$ at
   $k_\mathrm{min} r = 10^{-3}$ instead of $8.5 \times 10^{-4}$. Its sharper step has a
   slower spectral decay, which the output at small $r$ amplifies as $r^{-(1+b)}$ under a
   positive bias: for the Gaussian window, $F = 1$, $L = 10$, padding $0.3$ and $b = 1.8$,
   the second derivative at the smallest $r$ is still off by $2.3 \times 10^{-4}$ of its
   peak at 20000 knots, and a calibration to $10^{-7}$ does not converge. The end of the
   taper must also stay inside the rounded padding, which is at least $0.95\,h$ for the
   sizes a calibration visits (measured for $p = 0.3$ and $1$, $N \ge 100$).
4. **Letting the two ends overlap.** Continuing each end past the middle of the padding,
   blended with the other, reaches furthest ($6.8 \times 10^{-5}$ in the example of
   lever 3), but the blend then holds values of $f = F k^{-b}$ from both ends, whose
   $k^b$ differ by $e^{b L_T}$. It is safe only without a bias, and it moves with the
   rounded period of a fractional padding.

The tests `/ncm/fftlog/smooth_padding/negative_slope` and
`/ncm/fftlog/smooth_padding/refine_stable` measure the reach and the stability under
refinement; a change to the continuation should keep both.

## Bias

The transform represents $F$ by its Fourier series in $\ln k$, and its roundoff
scales with the dynamic range of what it represents, over the interval and the
padding. An $F$ that grows into a padding (for the variance of a power law
$P \propto k^n$, $F \propto k^{n+2}$ grows below $k_\mathrm{min}$ when $n < -2$)
sets a floor far above double precision: for the top-hat window and
$F \propto k^{-0.6}$ over 13 decades, the change from $N$ to $1.2N$ knots stalls at
$2.4 \times 10^{-6}$ of the peak. With a bias $b$
([[numcosmo-math|ncm_fftlog_set_bias]]) the series is of $f(k) = F(k) k^{-b}$
instead,
$$
G(r) = r^{-b} \int_0^\infty f(k)\,(kr)^b K(kr)\,\mathrm{d}k,
\qquad
Y_n = \int_0^\infty t^{\,b + \frac{2\pi i n}{L_T}} K(t)\,\mathrm{d}t,
$$
and each $\ln r$ derivative brings down $-(1 + b + 2\pi i n / L_T)$. $G$ is the same for
any $b$; the padding holds $f$, and the smooth continuation, fitted to $f$, gives the
same padded $F$. For a power law $F \propto k^b$, $f$ is constant; with the bias chosen as
below, $b = -0.40$, the example above converges to $10^{-11}$ at 8000 knots.

The coefficients exist only where $t^b K(t)$ is integrable: $-1 < b < 3$ for the
top-hat window, whose square falls as $t^{-4}$, and $b > -1$ for the Gaussian. Within
that range the bias moves two floors. The periodic image of the input one period away
enters with weight $e^{-(b - b_\mathrm{min}) L_T}$ at one end of the range and
$e^{-(b_\mathrm{max} - b) L_T}$ at the other, and a positive bias multiplies the
roundoff of the output at small $r$ by $r^{-(1+b)}$.
[[numcosmo-math|ncm_fftlog_get_best_bias]] therefore keeps $b = 0$ when $F$ decays
into both paddings, otherwise takes the value closest to zero between the log-slopes of
$F$ at the two ends (their midpoint when $F$ grows at both ends), and keeps it
$\ln(1/\epsilon)/L_T$ inside the range.

## Size

For efficiency, the requested $N(1 + p)$, with $p$ the padding fraction, is replaced by
the smallest $N_f^\prime \ge N(1 + p)$ that factorizes as $2^a 3^b 5^c 7^d$, with
$a,b,c,d$ non-negative integers. Each side then takes
$N_\mathrm{pad} = \lfloor N_f^\prime p / (2(1 + p)) \rfloor$ knots and the interval the
remaining $N^\prime = N_f^\prime - 2 N_\mathrm{pad}$, so the padding fraction actually used,
and with it $L_T = L N_f^\prime / N^\prime$, changes slightly with the size: for $p = 0.3$
and $L = 10$ around 3000 knots, $L_T$ is below $L(1 + p)$ by $1.7$ to
$6.2 \times 10^{-3}$. The taper of the smooth padding is placed on the nominal padding
$p L / 2$ so that it does not move with this rounding.

## Usage

The user provides $\ln k_0$, $\ln r_0$, $L$, the padding fraction, $N$, and the
function $F(k)$. The function can be supplied either as a `gsl_function`,
evaluated at the fundamental-interval knots, or as a vector of values computed at
each $\ln k$ knot; the padding is filled as described above.

The kernel-dependent coefficients $Y_n$ are provided by the concrete
implementations, e.g. [[numcosmo-math|NcmFftlogTophatwin2]] and
[[numcosmo-math|NcmFftlogGausswin2]].
